definition: The gradual degradation of a deployed model's performance over time as real-world data distributions shift away from the training data.
details: Model drift necessitates ongoing monitoring, evaluation, and periodic retraining or fine-tuning of production models to maintain performance as the environment and user behavior evolve.
story: Think of a hiker descending a foggy hill in the dark, taking small steps and feeling for the steepest way down. The machine starts out clumsy, makes mistakes, and is nudged a little less wrong every time. It is the same loop you use to learn anything: try, miss, correct, try again. Skill, for a model, is just error pushed down until it is small enough to ignore. That steady, miss-by-miss improvement is Model Drift.
